answer.rationale: The mandate forces action within 14 days since the incumbent won't reopen price and the contract won't auto-renew; the low-cost vendor's quote is the only option that meets the 18% cut alone, so switch_primary_vendor is the leading candidate. However, the line has zero volume buffer (94% committed), so any transition risk from onboarding a new primary supplier is amplified—delivery risk must not increase even while cost drops. memory_c2 is the single inherited claim asserting that this exact switch was low-risk (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) last time, but it's a consolidated summary without visible caveats about volume conditions or timeline pressure comparable to today's, so it's the highest-leverage memory to verify before committing capacity to this move. Given the no-buffer constraint, I'm scaling this as a small guarded test (e.g., phased ramp or dual-run before full cutover) rather than an immediate full switch, to protect delivery continuity while still capturing the cost benefit. Negotiate_terms already failed this cycle (consistent with c4 only applying at renewal windows with leverage, which we lack now); defer_decision isn't viable since the contract doesn't auto-renew and expires in 14 days; add_second_source doesn't by itself meet the mandate and takes longer to qualify than the runway allows, though it remains a fallback risk-mitigant noted via c3. Renew_incumbent is ruled out since they refused to reopen price and mandate isn't met.
